sources_read: .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r1/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx: Quality Checks row 6 ('One reasonable reading, and every capability is reachable from the seed, the provided runtime, or the public internet (network is allowed). (Reports every ambiguity/unreachable item.)') and Internal Quality Checks row 6 (says 'no network'; superseded by the skill's public-network delivery profile)
task/tests/app_context.md, tests/scored/functional/judge.toml (all 17 criteria) and prompt.md, tests/gates/constraints/prompt.md, tests/gates/render/prompt.md
evidence:
Reachability: Every capability is reachable. environment/Dockerfile installs Node 22 (node:22-bookworm-slim), express@5.1.0 and better-sqlite3@12.4.1 globally with NODE_PATH, matching integration.md; network_mode=public; seed /assets/kittle.json contains all accounts, matters, timers, walls, holds, versions and read_up_to positions the notes refer to; fixed clock is stated (integration.md) and in the seed. Seed arithmetic is consistent with the brief: K-10 at 2026-05-05T11:00:00Z is exactly 7 days old on 7-day M-11 (gone), K-11 one second younger (shown); K-1 (1 May) expired with surviving reply K-14 and held K-15; K-13 'Probate estimate' (4 May, 8 days) survives 30 days and dies at 7; 'Draft will sent for your review.' K-8 (10 May) survives the 7-day shortening that later criteria depend on; K-17 'Insurer letter' (3 May, held) disappears on release. No outside address is needed.

Defect (P0, achievability conflict between the public rule and the graded outcome): conversations.md:25 says 'When I open a matter, it shows a "new messages" line where I stopped reading'. Criterion unread_and_new_messages_line (tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:187) requires, after Harriet posts JUDGE-U1/U2, that when Dev opens M-13 'a "new messages" line sits just above JUDGE-U1'. Nothing in that criterion, or in any earlier criterion, has Dev open M-13 first. Seed read_up_to puts Dev at K-8 in M-13, so K-9 (Gwen's reply, 12 May 09:30) is already unread, and by criterion 13 earlier criteria have added unread M-13 messages from others: JUDGE-R0, R1, R2, R3, RX, R1B (nested_replies), JUDGE-E1 (edits), JUDGE-F1/F2 (safe_formatting). Under the only reasonable reading of 'where I stopped reading', the line belongs above K-9, not above JUDGE-U1. The golden does exactly that: app.js:186 'const firstUnread = r.data.messages.find(x => x.seq > r.data.last_read && !x.mine && !x.deleted)' with last_read = K-8's seq (server.js:119-122, 239-241). So a judge following the criterion literally fails the golden and every conforming app. The scripted golden harness only passes because it adds an unstated setup step: functional.cjs:337 'await openMatter(dev, 'M-13'); await openMatter(dev, 'M-11');' before posting, which does not appear in the criterion. Reverse case: a broken app that always draws the line above the newest-arriving batch, ignoring the stored read position, would pass.

Secondary ambiguity (P2): walls-and-retention.md:19 says a new wall applies to someone with the matter open 'the next time their screen refreshes'. A second reasonable reading is a manual page reload; the live-update list in conversations.md:31 (posts, replies, edits, disappearing messages) does not name wall changes. Criterion wall_added_live (judge.toml:79) requires the matter to vanish 'without reloading, wait up to ten seconds'. A server-enforced app that hides M-13 on the next reload and refuses Sian's post conforms to the reload reading yet fails. The golden polls, so this does not affect Oracle.

Minor note (no defect claimed): conversations.md:29 requires same-time messages to have 'one consistent order', while sent_once_in_order Part B requires the send order A, B, C. Send order is the natural reading for chat, and conversations.md:7 says replies are kept 'in the order they were sent', so I treat this as acceptable. Separately, outside this row: hold_scope_and_release requires a delete refusal, but the first delete success (message_links) runs later, which conflicts with the prompt rule that a refusal pairs with an earlier or same-criterion success. Other row reviewers should check this.

No configured judge run, Oracle or model score exists (raw-evidence-index scope says so). The P0 rests on source reading of the criterion, seed and golden, not on a measured judge failure.
counterexample: Golden as shipped: by criterion 13 Dev's stored M-13 read position is K-8. Per conversations.md:25 and app.js:186 the golden draws 'New messages' above K-9 'Received, reading it tonight.' (or the first earlier JUDGE message), so the line is not 'just above JUDGE-U1' and a literal judge fails unread_and_new_messages_line (weight 2.0 of 34 functional). Any conforming app does the same. For the wall: an app that enforces the wall on the server and drops M-13 on the next manual reload satisfies 'next time their screen refreshes' but fails wall_added_live's no-reload wait.
suggested_fix: In unread_and_new_messages_line, add a first step where Dev opens M-13 (marking it read) and returns to another matter before Harriet posts, as functional.cjs:337 already does, or require the line above Dev's first unread message instead of JUDGE-U1. In walls-and-retention.md:19, say the matter disappears from an open screen within a few seconds without reloading, or add wall changes to the live-update sentence in conversations.md:31.
